title: perf-watt-token-sensitivity-vignettes
content:
Summary: quick, informal vignette-based sensitivity analysis of token $/cost and perf-per-watt tradeoffs across A10, L4, A100, H100. This is a working sheet: measurements are from internal microbench runs (chat generation, 1:1 token emission), pre-aggregation, and include power draw sampling from PDUs. Purpose: give product + infra a handful of scenario recommendations for instance selection and autoscale policies.

Methods & assumptions:
- Baseline generation workload: autoregressive sampling, temperature 0.8, typical response length = 120 tokens, prompt prefix average 80 tokens. Two representative SLOs: low-latency (<100ms per token) and batch-friendly (throughput prioritized).
- Measurements: tokens/sec (steady-state), average GPU power (watts) measured by PDU during steady phase, and spot hourly cost assumed for instance rental. Tokens/hr = tokens/sec * 3600. $/token = $/hr / tokens/hr. perf/W = tokens/sec / watts.
- Price assumptions (rack rental, inclusive of host): A10 = $0.45/hr, L4 = $0.90/hr, A100 = $1.80/hr, H100 = $3.80/hr (these are internal list placeholders for sensitivity analysis).
- Quantization modes considered: FP16 baseline, INT8 (quant-friendly kernels) optimistic uplift.

Microbench table (rounded for readability):

Instance | tokens/sec | watts | tokens/sec/W | tokens/hr | $/hr | $/token | $/1k tokens | notes
A10      | 220        | 120   | 1.83         | 792,000   | 0.45 | 0.00000057 | 0.00057   | low-cost slot; good for small models and int8
L4       | 420        | 160   | 2.63         | 1,512,000 | 0.90 | 0.00000060 | 0.00060   | best perf/W for medium workloads; low power envelope
A100     | 900        | 300   | 3.00         | 3,240,000 | 1.80 | 0.00000056 | 0.00056   | predictable at scale; strong throughput for FP16
H100     | 1400       | 400   | 3.50         | 5,040,000 | 3.80 | 0.00000075 | 0.00075   | highest absolute throughput; cost sensitive at low utilization

Interpretation notes:
- Raw $/token in these numbers is surprisingly close across A10/L4/A100 for the baseline FP16 runs because throughput scales roughly with price in our pricing assumptions. H100 shows better perf/W but higher absolute $/hr, so $/token is higher at low utilization.
- Perf-per-watt (tokens/sec/W) favors H100 and A100; L4 sits in a sweet spot for perf/W when costs are constrained and host power budgets exist. A10 is efficient cost-per-hour but lower absolute throughput.
- INT8/quant uplift (observed): A10 and L4 show up to +30% tokens/sec with INT8 kernels for some models; A100/H100 show more modest +10–15% uplift unless model ops fully fused for tensor cores. When INT8 is applicable, A10 becomes notably competitive on $/1k tokens for small-medium workloads.

Vignettes (scenarios):

1) Small-scale chat feature (low concurrency, strict cost target)
- SLO: average latency under 200ms tail, target $/1k tokens < $0.001
- Recommendation: single A10 with INT8 quantized model; burst to L4 for periodic traffic spikes. Rationale: A10 gives cheapest seat and INT8 uplift keeps $/token under threshold for typical short responses.
- Risks: INT8 quality regressions; fallback to FP16 increases $/k tokens ~20–40%.

2) High-throughput summarization pipeline (batching allowed)
- SLO: throughput prioritized, latency per batch acceptable up to seconds.
- Recommendation: A100 cluster with large batch sizes and KV caching. Rationale: A100 cost scales well with batching; stable $/token and highest overall throughput for pooled pipelines. Consider spot pricing and reserved capacity.

3) Enterprise SLA-chat (predictable latency & capacity)
- SLO: 95th latency < 150ms, predictable capacity for enterprise customers
- Recommendation: Dedicated L4 fleet for production steady-state + H100 for overflow (canary for simulator workloads). Rationale: L4 gives good perf/W and predictable cost; H100 reserved for large concurrent events where absolute throughput needed.

4) Latency-sensitive creative generation (long contexts)
- SLO: maintain low tail latency for long sequences (>=2048 tokens)
- Recommendation: H100 or A100 pinned instances (prioritize H100 if long-context kernels and fused attention optimized). Rationale: higher memory and throughput for long KV cache operations; cost amortized over long outputs.

Sensitivity runs (quick math):
- Price shock +/-20% on $/hr: for A100, +20% price -> $/1k increases from 0.00056 to ~0.00067. For H100 the same shock has a larger absolute effect on billing and pushes some use-cases over economical thresholds.
- Throughput variance -10%: if H100 throughput drops 10% (e.g., thermal throttling), $/1k jumps from 0.00075 to ~0.00083. H100 is more sensitive to perf volatility because of the higher baseline cost.

Operational notes & questions:
- Need a standard benchmark harness that reproduces these metrics (we used local harness v2 but results vary by model family). Action: eng/bench to produce canonical scripts + seed data (ENG-4521).
- Power sampling cadence: current PDUs sampled at 1s resolution. Verify with infra for 100ms granularity for better per-request attribution.
- Model family effects: our bench runs used a GPT-family 7B-ish model. Larger models shift perf/W and int8 applicability differently. Add 13B and 70B runs.

Recommendations (short):
- Ship a small playbook for customers: "When to choose L4 vs A100 vs H100" — emphasize perf/W, utilization expectations, and quantization caveats.
- Default autoscale policy: prefer L4 for steady workloads, A100 for predictable batched ML pipelines, H100 only for sustained high-concurrency or long-context uses. Allow A10 for cost-sensitive dev/alpha environments with explicit quality flags.
- Include perf/W as a first-class metric in Console cost breakdowns (tokens/sec/W and $/1k tokens).

To-do / next steps:
- Validate numbers on 13B family and with 2 more runs for INT8 (Mariana).
- Add raw CSVs + PDU logs to linked_artifacts and canonicalize harness (Ethan).
- Convert this vignette sheet into a short one-pager for Solutions engineering and GTM.
